{"requested_url": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sudofx/wake/85c611dfcb54e4918d7023e7cd07aec7f27dc14a/docs/architecture.md", "source_revision": "85c611dfcb54e4918d7023e7cd07aec7f27dc14a", "running_revision": "8e6574128486bc628b98e8b43e90544bd0d50569", "source_search": "", "url": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sudofx/wake/85c611dfcb54e4918d7023e7cd07aec7f27dc14a/docs/architecture.md", "scope": "raw source-controlled WAKE repository text", "excerpt": "# Architecture and limits

See [the reusable kernel contract](kernel.md) for application ownership and the
non-research execution proof, and [installation boundaries](installations.md) for
independent records and runtime lifecycles. These remain inside this repository.

The local [improvement application](improvements.md) uses that same kernel contract
in an explicitly new experiment record. Captured public research informs code
proposals; it does not become writable research authority. Untrusted candidate
code runs only in restricted disposable containers, while the host scores its
outputs. An operator review receipt cannot apply code or grant release authority.

The [autonomous context lane](autonomous-context.md) is a separate WAKE application
policy on the existing per-node native authority. An installed capability permits
one selector-field change, gated by recomputed fixed-task and current-native-state
measurements. Proposal generation, adoption and rollback require no per-change
human review. Metadata events preserve research versions and history; candidate
data cannot replace the evaluator, widen permissions, modify code or create a
competing research store. Native replay owns the policy after restart.

> **Current specification.** This document explains why the present system is shaped this way: its trust boundary, durable record, governance model and known limits. Current local procedures belong in `standalone.md`; public mirror publishing belongs in `cloud.md`. Maintainer navigation, environment checks and reproducible validation guidance belong in `development.md`.

**WAKE✳︎** is infrastructure for continuity of accountable work, not continuity of a model instance. Its stable sequence is **Record → Context → Proposal → Governance → Transition → Receipt**. Drawing on qualitative interviews and ethnographic data from three school development processes in Germany, we reconstruct organizational re-combination processes from a differentiation-theoretical perspective. Rather than applying the theory subsumptively, we employ social-ontological and society-theoretical concepts in a reflexive oscillation between empirical and theoretical enrichment. Along the horizontal and vertical axes of Luhmannian system(-level) differentiation, we systematize translation cascades and identify two polycontextural complications that only become analytically accessible through systematic analysis of code dynamics and operational couplings. At the first-order level, \\\"contingency incongruence\\\" emerges as competency-based learning concepts encounter a binary-coded contingency of the established program. Interorganizational workshops convened between schools and consultancing organizations to address this reveal a second-order complication: The \\\"a-addressability\\\" of workshop participants renders the intervention unreachable beyond the boundaries of the emergent third system.
